data_classification: Hand-authored synthetic fixtures; no customer or employer data.
scope: Direct local Python handler calls with actual SQLite state. No AWS, queue, network, UI, or outbox dispatcher.

rules: The event has exactly request_id, sku, and quantity fields.
request_id and sku are strings of 1..64 characters; quantity is an integer 1..100, never a boolean.
A new request returns status created and an order_id, and persists exactly one order with status created.
The same key and payload return status existing with the original order_id; storage must not grow.
The same key with different sku or quantity returns status conflict without order_id; storage must not change.
Invalid events return status invalid_input and must not create orders.
Exactly one nonempty string order_id is required.
A known order returns status fulfilled and its order_id; its persisted status becomes fulfilled.
The first fulfillment inserts one OrderFulfilled outbox row.
Sequential duplicate fulfillment returns the same success shape but MUST NOT insert a second outbox row.
A missing order returns status not_found and leaves both tables unchanged.
A local-only observation adapter returns status observed, orders array, and outbox array.
An optional order_id string filters both arrays; an empty event observes all persisted rows.
Order rows include order_id, request_id, sku, quantity, status.
Outbox rows include event_id, order_id, event_type.
Use storage assertions after processing, rather than relying solely on handler responses.

invariants: Each scenario starts with empty storage and never depends on a previous scenario.
Use $from references to pass created order identifiers across steps.
A fulfilled order produces one outbox event even when sequential requests repeat.
Rejected input leaves persisted state unchanged.
Positive and negative workflows must retain meaningful explicit assertions.
